title: Enrollment deadlines for the 2025/2026 academic year
content: The standard enrollment period opens on July 1 and closes on July 20. The late registration period runs from September 1 to September 10 and incurs an administrative late fee of $30. Applications submitted after the deadline are not processed without a justified cause accredited by the Registrar's Office.

title: Tuition fees and installment plans
content: The tuition fee depends on the number of enrolled credits and the number of attempts consumed for each course. Tuition can be paid in full, or divided into two or eight installments. The installment plan must be requested at the exact time of enrollment; subsequent modifications are not permitted.

title: Partial enrollment cancellation
content: Partial cancellation of enrolled courses can be requested until October 31. This does not generate a refund of the paid amount unless the cancellation is due to an error attributable to the university administration. Total cancellation follows a different procedure.

title: Credit recognition for extracurricular activities
content: Up to 6 credits can be recognized for cultural, sports, student representation, or volunteering activities. The request must be submitted to the Registrar's Office along with a certificate from the organizing entity. Recognized credits do not carry a numerical grade on the transcript.

title: Requirements for curricular internships
content: To apply for curricular internships, the student must have successfully completed at least 120 credits of the degree program and be enrolled in the internship course during the academic year in which they are taking place. Applications from students failing to meet both requirements will be rejected.

title: Duration and schedule of internships
content: Curricular internships have a total duration of 300 hours, which correspond to 12 academic credits. The daily schedule cannot exceed 5 hours when the student has mandatory on-campus classes, nor 7 hours during periods without classes.

title: Academic and company supervisors
content: Every intern is assigned an academic supervisor from the university and a professional supervisor designated by the collaborating company. The academic supervisor evaluates the final internship report; the company supervisor issues a performance report that accounts for 40 percent of the final grade.

title: Extracurricular internships
content: Extracurricular internships are voluntary and are not part of the standard degree curriculum. They are recorded on the student's Co-Curricular Transcript. Their maximum duration is 750 hours per academic year and they require a prior formal agreement between the university and the hosting entity.

title: General Federal Financial Aid
content: The general federal grant application is usually published in March and the deadline is in May. Family income thresholds and academic requirements are updated in each call. Applications must be submitted electronically via the Department of Education's portal.

title: Departmental Collaboration Grants
content: The collaboration grant is aimed at senior undergraduate and master's students. It requires a minimum GPA of 3.25 for Engineering and Architecture programs. The commitment is three hours per day during the academic year.

title: University Emergency Funds
content: The university offers its own financial aid for unforeseen emergencies: loss of employment of the primary provider, severe illness, or unexpected family burdens. These funds are compatible with general federal grants and are resolved within two months after the application deadline.

title: Causes for scholarship revocation
content: A scholarship will be revoked if the student fails to pass the minimum required percentage of credits, if they cancel their enrollment, or if it is discovered that the provided information was falsified. Revocation implies the mandatory reimbursement of all received funds.

title: Academic standing and continuation policy
content: A full-time undergraduate student must pass at least 30 percent of their enrolled credits during their first year. Otherwise, they will not be allowed to continue in the same degree program, although they may request readmission after one full academic year has passed.

title: Grading system and exam attempts
content: Each course offers two examination attempts per academic year. A student has the right to a maximum of six attempts per course over their academic career. The fifth and sixth attempts can be evaluated by a special academic committee if the student requests it 15 days in advance.

title: Exam reviews and grade appeals
content: Professors must publish the review date alongside the provisional grades. Students have seven calendar days from the publication date to submit a formal, justified appeal to the department chair.

title: Senior Capstone Project regulations
content: The Senior Capstone Project is defended before a three-member academic panel. In order to defend it, the student must have passed all other required credits of the degree program. The written thesis must be submitted fifteen days prior to the defense date.

title: Academic Integrity Code
content: Plagiarism, identity fraud, and the undeclared use of external assistance (including AI) in evaluations constitute severe academic offenses. Consequences range from a failing grade in the course to the opening of a formal disciplinary expulsion process.

title: Institutional password recovery
content: The institutional account password can be reset from the university's identity portal using the configured two-factor authentication (2FA). If the student has lost access to their 2FA, they must visit the IT Helpdesk in person with a valid photo ID.

title: Accessing the campus Wi-Fi network
content: The campus network uses 802.1X authentication with institutional credentials. The user ID must be entered in its full format, including the @oakhaven-university.edu domain. The institutional password must never be shared with third parties under any circumstances.

title: Opening an IT support ticket
content: Technical issues must be registered through the IT support portal. Each ticket receives a unique tracking identifier. High-priority issues, such as an examination server crash, are addressed within a maximum timeframe of four business hours.

title: Cloud storage and institutional email
content: The institutional account includes email and enterprise cloud storage. The storage quota is reduced by half six months after graduation and the account is entirely deleted after twelve months. The student is responsible for exporting their data before that deadline.

title: Requesting official academic transcripts
content: Official personal academic transcripts are requested through the student portal and are issued with a digital signature within five business days. A certified transcript for international use requires apostille legalization and takes up to fifteen business days to be issued.

title: Updating personal data in the academic record
content: The modification of personal data must be requested at the Registrar's Office by providing supporting legal documentation. Legal name and gender marker changes are processed according to current legislation and do not require a medical report.

title: Transferring records to another university
content: Transferring an academic record requires an official admission letter from the destination university and the payment of the transfer fee. The home university has one month to send the official transcript once the fee is paid.
